key_insight: UV disinfection of virus-laden saliva droplets cannot be modeled accurately without accounting for droplet-dependent UV scattering, which creates strongly non-uniform exposure and changes virus inactivation.
engineering_relevance: The CFD-DDA platform can help design more effective UV air purification systems by predicting how droplet size, shape, airflow, and walls affect surviving viral copies.
method: Couples CFD for droplet evaporation and transport with DDA for UV light scattering.
Handles both spherical droplets and irregular evaporated droplet shapes in 3D.
Introduces the Dbouk-Yurkin law, extending Chick-Watson to include UV scattering effects.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a coupled Euler-Lagrange CFD-DDA evaluation of initial droplet distribution, airflow rate, and wall interactions to quantify surviving coronavirus copies Ns under specified conditions.
watch_item: The model depends on assumptions such as a 100 nm virion diameter, fixed temperature and humidity, and idealized scattering behavior, so real-world validation and parameter sensitivity are important.
paper_title: An Innovative Computational Fluid Dynamics Discrete Dipole Approximation (CFD-DDA) Platform for Predicting Airborne Virus-in-Saliva Disinfection by Ultraviolet Irradiation
